title: HW Loop Parent-to-Child Reheat Load Response
description: Starts the complete Boiler-1 circulation and firing path, establishes AHU/VAV airflow, stages two VAV reheat coils, and then removes their load so students can trace valve position through flow, differential pressure, HWS/HWR delta, boiler firing, and discharge-air temperature.

events.description: Start Boiler-1 purge and ignition sequence
Stage the first reheat load after HW temperature and pressure establish
Add a second child load and observe aggregate loop response
Remove the second load and observe loop recovery and pump-only heat

expected_results: Distribution flow and differential pressure appear when the HW pump proves, before burner heat is available
Each valve stage increases child coil flow/load, lowers common HWR relative to HWS, and raises the associated VAV discharge temperature
Boiler firing and heat output increase in response to the return-water/load disturbance rather than jumping instantly
Closing both valves removes coil load while pump heat, piping losses, water inventory, and temperature coast remain visible
completion_criteria: Student traces the causal chain from valve command to actuator stroke, branch flow, coil BTUH, HWR, boiler firing, and DAT
Student explains why pump proof alone creates flow and heat but cannot maintain HWS setpoint without a proven burner
instructor_notes: Recommended at 10x for a roughly 48-second demonstration. The command center's proof allowance uses simulated time and its failure confirmation uses wall time, so acceleration does not create false start failures. Use RESTART before a graded repeat when identical thermal initial conditions matter.
student_objectives: Read a hot-water system as a coupled energy and hydraulic loop
Distinguish parent availability, child demand, actuator travel, and thermal transport delay
